purpose.description: Registry of all interfaces in the evaluated lattice that satisfy target identifiability.
purpose.role: Characterize the sufficient region above the identifiability frontier.
not_used_for: claiming all sufficient interfaces are optimal

sufficiency_frontier.definition: Interfaces satisfying factorization with no strictly cheaper sufficient predecessor.

non_frontier_examples.reason: Adds temporal information after sufficiency is already achieved.
Adds intervention diversity without increasing target access.

refinement_analysis.observation: Sufficient interfaces form an upward-closed region under the refinement relation.
refinement_analysis.interpretation: Once target-relevant distinctions are preserved, additional information is unnecessary for identifiability but may improve robustness.

robustness_note.statement: A non-minimal interface may outperform the minimum under finite data or noise without being required for factorization.

decision.meaning: The sufficient interface region has been enumerated and its minimal frontier identified.

notes: Sufficiency is not the same as optimality.
The minimal interface defines the lowest information cost for the declared target.
Higher-cost interfaces may become preferable when moving from exact identifiability to approximate estimation.
